CHINA MAIL
Poppy day in Singapore resulted in the collection of about $16,000, including $4,000 which had been received before Poppy Day began. First year the collection was $22,000.

label: text
text: Rueben, the British Indian hotel runner who has been sentenced to life-long imprisonment in connection with the murder of Mrs. Macfie in a hotel in Garoet. Java, is to appeal against his sentence.

label: text
text: It is probable that an air line will soon link London and Paris with North Africa. The Air Union will most likely absorb the French Compagnie Aeronavale, which has run a flying boat service from France to forsiam for some time past.

label: text
text: As a result of house searches in Sourabaya following on the riots there two teachers of the so-called “proletarian school” have been suspended, as it has been proved that they are in communication with communists in Canton.

label: text
text: The British Bloodhound aeroplane, which with its Jupiter engine recently carried out a 25,000-mile flight test without replacement, followed this up by a flight from Ceyond to Cairo in 50 hours. The only replacements after the 27,000 miles were one valve and a spring.

label: text
text: A South African deputation will visit the Dutch Indies's report on the possibilities of trade and shipping between the two countries. The Premier General Hertzog, chief the South African Minister of Finance, now favourably inclined towards the proposals and it is expected that the Union Government will shortly authorise the expense. An invitation to visit Malaysia may be extended.

label: text
text: Mr. A. W. Still writes to the "Strait Times" from London on October 14: — British trade continues to suffer deplorably from the prolonged coal strike, but the old country is bearing its trial spendily. It is not downhearted, and is ready to make up for lost time as soon as the miners recover their sanity. Now that the cold weather is coming, a good many of them, deprived of their usual supplies of domestic fuel, are beginning to realise that one section of the community cannot hurt others without hurting itself.

label: text
text: The ship's company of H.M.S. "Despatch" held an enjoyable and successful dance at the King Edward Hotel last night. There was a good attendance.

label: text
text: The Sourubayn Chamber of Commerce will celebrate its seventy-fifth anniversary on December 13.

label: text
text: The public is cordially invited to attend a free lecture at the old Chamber of Commerce Room, City Hall, at 5.45 p.m. on December 7, by Mr. John Randall Dunn, C.S.B. of Boston, U.S.A. under the auspices of First Church of Christ, Scientist, Hong Kong.

label: text
text: Members and guests are reminded that practice dances for St. Andrew's Ball will be held at the City Hall on Tuesday. November 23 and Friday, November 28 from 5 to 7 p.m. Members are requested to send in their lists of guests.

label: text
text: Burning of bodies as they are recovered has been begun in Batangus; where more than 100 bodies have been found underneath the rainy left by the recent typhoon and flood, says the “Munilla Bulletin.” Those which are being recovered now are unrecognisable, and sanitation and prevention of disease has become the paramount consideration.

label: text
text: A sailor was injured on board the Chinese steamer "Wong Shek Kung" on her return journey from Suigon to Hong Kong.

label: text
text: Four cases of notifiable disease occurred in the Colony on Thursday. One was in British case of diphtheria from the city. The other three patients had enteric fever (typhoid); two were Chinese and one British, two cases being from the city and the other from Shaukiwan.

label: text
text: The police at Sawah, Loentoc, Java, have succeeded, after months of difficult work, in discovering an extensive "communist plot." The conspirators are from Solok, Melaloe and Sawah Loentoe. Reports state that 200 sabres have been imported from Melaloe, and the communists were divided into groups of which Ramaja, who is at present under arrest, was the "major." The object of the plot says the "Singapore Free Press" correspondent, was the murder of all officials: 140 sabres were seized by the police working in conjunction with the field police, and all the leaders have been arrested.

label: text
text: Directions have been given that Vice-Admiral Sir Reginald Tyrwhitt, whose selection to be Commander-in-Chief in China was announced on September 24, was to hoist his flag in the "President" on November 8, his presence being dispensed with, and it was to be struck at sunset on the same day. Sir Reginald will then be regarded as on leave of absence until he proceeds to take up his appointment, which will be about January 7, 1927.

label: doc_title
text: "SOCIAL " AND PERSONAL " NEWS.

label: text
text: Mr. S. B. Carr, assistant manager of the Ford Motor Company of Japan, died at St. Luke's International Hospital, Nagasaki.

label: text
text: On October 29, a banquet was given at the Moderne Hotel, Harbin, to the assistant manager of the Chinese Eastern Railway, Mr. A.H. Kallina, who has been in railway service for 25 years. Not only railway officials and servants attended, but also many prominent commercial men, the total number of guests being 336. The whole of the halls of the hotel were made use of for this occasion only. Many of the guests made a night of it, only returning home to breakfast.

label: text
text: Mr. G. N. Farquhar has left Kurnegalle, Ceylon, for Nuwara Eliya to assume duties as District Judge, and Mr. Davidson has succeeded him as Office Assistant to the Government Agent, N.W.P.

label: text
text: Among the candidates declared by the Admiralty to have been successful in the professional examination for warrant supply officer, held in July last, were P. G. Hopping, "Ambrose" (previously qualified in victualling and mathematics), and G. Best, of the "Mantis," passed in mathematics and victualling.

label: text
text: The following appointments were made by the Admiralty on October 14:—Commdr. C. C. B. Vacher, to “Dahlia,” in command (on commg.), and to “Cornflower,” in command (on transfer). Lieut.-Commr. C. Caslon, to “Hawkins,” addl. (November 10), and as Flag. Lieut. to V/A Sir R. Y. Tyrwhitt, and as Fleet (S) Officer and W/T Officer (on transfer of flag).

label: text
text: The Prince of Wales has become patron of the Ross Institute and Hospital for Tropical Diseases.

label: text
text: Commissioner " F. W. Pearce, leader of the Salvation Army in North China, passed away on November 4.

label: text
text: The famous Chinese female impersonator, Mei Lan-fang, arrived in Shanghai from Peking on November 7.

label: text
text: There will be a public lecture at the Helena May Institute on Monday, November 22 at 5.30 p.m. given by Mr. D. O. de Silva Subject: — "Japan." Admission free.—Advt.

label: text
text: For what was probably the first time on record it was necessary to abandon the Charter Day celebrations in Jesselton owing to the unspeakable weather. First it was decided to abandon a cricket match, then the golf competition for the Straits Cup, and finally the Charter Day Parade itself.

label: text
text: Plans are being prepared for a North Sea airway to link the English east coast and Gothenburg by way of the Kiel Canal and the Kattegat. Harwich will be the British terminus. Southampton-Napier all-metal flying boats will be used, and the journey is to be made in one day.

label: text
text: A group of prominent Japanese businessesmen, including Messrs. Seimosuke Gow, Kaichiro Nezu and Shintaro Qhashi, have planned an express electric railway to run between Tokyo and Osaka in six hours and have applied for permission to the authorities who, however, consider this plan to be impracticable.

label: text
text: An extraordinary general meeting of the Hong Kong Philharmonic Society was held at St. John's Cathedral Hall last evening, to discuss matters pertaining to the forthcoming presentation of the "The Pirates of Penzance" at the Theatre Royal early in December. The proceedings were private.

label: text
text: A Lascar, named Samandar, who is in Pentonville prison under sentence of death for the murder of a shipmate in his bunk on the F, and O, steamer "China" while in Tilbury Dock on July 9 last, appealed in the Court of Criminal Appeal on Oct. 18 against his conviction. His appeal was dismissed.

label: text
text: Mr. L. A. Lyall, former Commissioner of Customs, Shanghai, was the guest at the Union Club tiffin on November 9.

label: text
text: Mr. S. Aoki, judge of the Japanese Consular Court in Shanghai, has been appointed Judge for Hand-chow, Soochow, Nanking and Wushi.

label: text
text: Owing to the venue not being indicated on the printed announcement, it was inadvertently stated yesterday that the Victoria Diocesan Association Sunday, observances would be at the Cathedral. A card received subsequently, "at St. Andrew's Church," Kowloon." At the close of morning prayer the Bishop of Victoria will unveil a memorial tablet to the late Hon. Sir C. P. Chatter.

label: text
text: Capt. F. R. Kennedy, I.A., has qualified as an interpreter, first class, in Chinese, as a result of the last examination in foreign languages.

label: text
text: Mr. Allan Béven, C.C.S., has assumed duties as District Judge of Kurnegalle, Ceylon, relieving Mr. G. Furse Roberts, who has been transferred to Negombo.

label: text
text: The Birthday of Sir Guoro Nanak Day Ji will be celebrated at the Sikh Temple to-day, and heads of departments and private firms have been requested to grant a holiday to their Sikh employees.

label: text
text: Mr. Julean Arnold, U.S. Commercial Attache, spoke at the meeting of the Literary Department of the American Women's Club, Shanghai, on November 9, on "China in America." Those who have heard Mr. Arnold in his former talks before the Club realise how much he has given on China, and this talk was of particular interest at this time.

label: text
text: Dating from October 15, Commander H. R. Moore, D.S.O., was relieved as executive officer of the cruiser "Delhi," in which he has served during the past two years, by Commander H. S. Bowlby, date of the Signal Department, Admiralty, and formerly in the "Renown" during the tour of the Prince of Wales to India and Japan.

label: text
text: A Reuter cable from San Francisco announces the death of George Sterling, the American Socialist poet.

label: text
text: A reminder is hardly necessary for the annual fete of the Hong Kong Women's Guild and the Ministering Children League at Government House to-morrow. The laudable object and the reputation of the organisers as entertainers are sufficient recommendation. Full particulars have been given by advertisement.

label: text
text: The following, forthcoming weddings are announced:—William Emil Greenbaum, lawyer, of Hoils Phil Islands to Delphine Bradt, the Lookout, Mountain, Team, U.S.A., and Oswald Fox, mercantile marine officer, of the China Navigation Company, Ltd., to Constance Mary Sorby, "en route to the Colony by the s.s. "Aeneas."

label: text
text: The Rev. B. S. Bonsall, of Wuchang, after some difficulties in the war zone, has finally got safely away. "He is a passenger by the North German Lloyd "Schlisien" which made a brief call at Woosung on November 8. Mr. Bonsall has been co-operating with the Christian Literature Society and his first book has just come from the Press, namely, "A Manual of Christian Doctrine," by the late Dr. Joseph Banks, for 30 years a teacher in the Theological College at Headingly, Leeds.

label: text
text: The death is announced of Towkay Foong Wah at Serendah, at the age of 71. Mr. Foong Wah was born in Canton in the year 1855 and came to Serendah in 1890, where he spent most of his life as merchant, miner and planter. He was also Managing Director of the Malayan Hydraulic Tin Mines, Ltd. for a number of years. Charities which he had helped include the Methodist Boys' School of Kuala Lumpur, The Child Welfare Society of Singapore, The Kwong Wai Siew Free Hospital, Nan Hua Girls School, Singapore, and the Yeung Ching School, Singapore. The funeral, which took place, Serendah on November 5, was largely attended by Europeans and Chinese. He leaves a widow, four sons and several grandchildren. "Straits Times."
